A comprehensive framework for computationally efficient system-level design optimization of machine tools
abstract: Mass reduction of machine tool components is a crucial task that can improve performance, accuracy, and energy efficiency. System-level optimization, where multiple components are simultaneously optimized, is noted in the literature as a challenging necessity for complete performance improvement of machine tools. Existing methods focus on optimizing the machine tool components individually, neglecting the critical effects of simultaneous modification on the machine performance and thorough exploration of the design space. To the authors’ knowledge, for the first time in the literature, this paper presents a comprehensive framework for system-level machine tool design optimization considering the most significant multi-objective performance indicators for the machining process. Static and dynamic stiffness, thermal and dynamic stability, and fatigue life are evaluated as performance indicators using a multi-objective finite element response set that includes coupled thermal-structural, modal, and frequency response analyses. A minimal parameter set approach is proposed which uses the linear guide joints to minimize the number of design variables, addressing the challenge of increased computational cost in system-level modeling. Machine responses during optimization iterations are predicted by a machine learning model trained on the machine tool’s multi-objective finite element response set, achieving higher accuracy than commonly used polynomial-based methods. A constraint relaxation method is proposed that permits limited degradation relative to the base design, yielding designs that substantially outperform those obtained from unconstrained optimization while avoiding over-constraining. Up to 20 % mass reduction is achieved across the machine tool components while the performance indicators are either improved or maintained with negligible degradation.

title: Spatial information bottleneck graph structure learning based multivariate time series prediction for industrial processes
A Human–Robot collaborative framework for draping of advanced composite materials
abstract: Manual draping carbon fibre and fibreglass plies is a critical yet labour-intensive step in composite manufacturing, where production efficiency and part quality strongly depend on operator skill and repeatability. This paper addresses the challenges of introducing Human–Robot Collaboration (HRC) to support draping operations while maintaining flexibility, safety, and industrial feasibility. The system featured intuitive human–robot interaction through a human action recognition system, a context reasoner, and a human–robot collaborative transport module designed for manipulating planar deformable objects. The framework was validated on two robotic workcells addressing three industrial use cases from the aerospace, automotive and maritime sectors. An extensive experimental campaign, culminating in the production of multi-layer components, demonstrated substantial gains in efficiency and operator support: process time for large components was reduced by 50%, while operator workload decreased by 40%. The robot’s precision in material placement also cut ply draping time per layer from 12% in manual operations to 6%, contributing to lower physical and cognitive demands on operators (workload scores averaging below 30%). The study shows that the benefits of HRC in draping operations are highly context-dependent: partial automation yields limited gains for small/medium components, whereas for large components it significantly improves performance by reducing cycle time, enhancing product quality, and minimising ergonomic strain on operators. Finally, the paper presents a critical analysis of the proposed solution, highlighting its drawbacks and suggesting improvements.

title: A double-sided bundle auction mechanism for collaborative additive manufacturing
abstract: Collaborative manufacturing has become an essential strategy for improving resource utilization and profitability in the additive manufacturing (AM) industry. In this study, we propose an additive manufacturing collaboration platform (AMCP) to facilitate bilateral resource exchange in decentralized AM environments. To address the challenges posed by the two-way, many-to-many exchange of heterogeneous AM resources in AMCP, we design a five-phase double-sided bundle auction (DBA) mechanism. This mechanism is proven to satisfy incentive compatibility, individual rationality, budget balance, and allocative efficiency, ensuring fair and efficient collaboration among self-interested participants. To optimize the winner determination problem in DBA, which arises from overlapping transactions and flexible bundle bidding, we reformulate it as a maximum weight independent set problem in graph theory. Based on this reformulation, we develop a graph-based adaptive neighborhood search algorithm that balances computational efficiency and solution quality. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed mechanism is both feasible and robust. It achieves superior social welfare, cooperation rates, and scalability when compared to traditional approaches. Additionally, sensitivity analysis reveals the robustness and resilience of the proposed mechanism, even in the presence of strategic manufacturers. • Propose an AM collaboration platform for decentralized resource exchange. • Design a five-phase double-sided bundle auction ensuring fairness and efficiency. • Reformulate the winner determination problem using graph-based theory. • Develop an adaptive algorithm balancing computational efficiency and accuracy. • Validate the auction’s robustness and scalability through experiments.

title: Corrigendum to “Automated extraction of comprehensive digital twin models for smart manufacturing systems” [J. Manuf. Syst. 85 (2026) 287–306]
The end-to-end real-time scheduling method for hybrid flow shop based on heterogeneous cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Personalized customization increases the complexity of the hybrid flow shop production environment, which is characterized by the presence of variable discrete events. The buffer capacities of machines and the transportation times between processing stages and the warehouse influence the overall production process. Therefore, the research problem addressed in this paper is the real-time scheduling problem for hybrid flow shops with limited buffers and transportation time. To effectively tackle this challenging scheduling problem, this paper proposes a discrete-event-driven heterogeneous cooperative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (HC-MADRL) framework. Within this framework, two types of heterogeneous scheduling agents are designed: the Job Agent (JA) and Stage-Machine Agents (SMAs). The JA employs an integrated LSTM-Pointer Network (LPN) architecture to select the most appropriate job based on the current job sequence states in real time. In contrast, the SMAs utilize a Transformer-based weighted network (TWN) incorporating a machine mask mechanism to assign the selected job to the optimal machine according to the state of its processing stage. Then, eight real-time job states and five generic stage-machine states are designed for the JA and SMAs, respectively. Meanwhile, a multi-level reward mechanism with reward shaping is proposed to guide the agents in learning to optimize the scheduling objective. Based on this, this paper presents an independent multi-agent proximal policy optimization (I-MAPPO) training algorithm that integrates two critic networks for heterogeneous multi-agent systems. Lastly, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior scheduling performance and real-time responsiveness compared with four benchmark real-time scheduling methods: PDRs, DQN, PPO, MAPPO and other two advanced multi-agent schedulers.

title: Heterogeneous multi-agent fleet control system for material handling in a Software-Defined Factory
abstract: The conventional Industry 4.0 architecture of manufacturing and warehousing is hardware-centric, limiting flexibility and adaptability. The material handling systems deploy heterogeneous multiple agents that have an application or environment-specific discrete control layer. This work presents the concept of a Software-Defined Factory and its control system for a software-centric control. The software-defined factory integrates industrial hardware and software systems, hosting the control system, AI, simulation, and digital twins to enable seamless material flow throughout the factory through heterogeneous multi-agent control. The presented control system has a centralized architecture designed with a bottom-up approach for commercial systems. It manages communication, localization, navigation, and task allocation in a heterogeneous multi-vendor fleet deployed in real-world scenarios. The latency, accuracy, repeatability, planning-level scalability, and path execution evaluations of the proposed system were conducted with heterogeneous fleets. The operation of overhead hoist transport vehicles with automated guided vehicles on a scaled semiconductor manufacturing shop floor demonstrated heterogeneous hardware integration for material handling in industrial settings. The proposed system has potential to mitigate major challenges in deployment, data interoperability, and hardware dependency for diverse industrial applications, including manufacturing, warehousing, and inspection.

title: From insight to action: Embodied multi-agent system integrating vision language model for digital twin-assisted human-robot collaborative assembly
abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly has emerged as a core pivotal technology for the high-efficiency manufacturing of complex products. Nevertheless, existing systems still face critical challenges: the difficulty in translating unstructured user assembly intent into standardized task execution, insufficient scenario-specific perceptual understanding of assembly contexts, and the lack of robust safety guarantees and intuitive operational guidance. To address these critical challenges, a novel embodied multi-agent system (MAS) integrated with a vision-language model (VLM) for digital twin (DT)-enabled HRC assembly is proposed in this paper, which constructs a closed-loop workflow encompassing multi-modal perception and reasoning (“insight”) as well as autonomous robot execution and collaboration (“action”). First, a collaborative embodied multi-agent framework is constructed to encompass task management, perception, reasoning, robot execution, and augmented reality (AR) execution, enabling seamless transition from unstructured assembly intent to standardized HRC implementation. Second, domain knowledge fine-tuning is performed on the VLM to achieve end-to-end understanding of visual inputs and semantic alignment with textual descriptions in assembly scenarios, thereby providing precise scenario-adapted perceptual support. Third, a cyber-physical mapping environment is built using DT technology to facilitate simulation verification of robot motion planning and real-time scene mapping for AR-guided operations. The experimental results verify that the proposed system effectively mitigates the limitations of existing HRC assembly systems, enabling efficient, adaptive, and safe collaborative assembly while laying a solid foundation for the intelligent upgrading of complex product assembly processes.

title: A Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph retrieval-augmented generation framework for intelligent maintenance
abstract: As industrial equipment is increasingly applied in manufacturing, it is necessary to adopt advanced maintenance techniques to ensure stable equipment operation. Maintenance decision support is essential for industrial equipment, but information fragmentation and complex reasoning hinder its progress. To address these challenges, we propose MAKG (Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph), a framework that synergizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a multi-agent system for intelligent industrial equipment maintenance. The MAKG framework uses these Large Language Models (LLM) agents to work together, drawing information from a diverse knowledge base to produce coordinated responses to equipment faults. Our method focuses on fine-tuning the embedding models with domain-specific data. This approach avoids the high computational cost of re-training the entire LLM and improves performance in the specific industrial context. In the experimental study, the MAKG framework was validated using real-world industrial operation and maintenance data, achieving a reasoning accuracy of 90.1% and demonstrating its potential for intelligent maintenance of industrial equipment. Code is available at https://github.com/LAM2360/MAKG_demo/tree/master.

title: A digital twin-enabled system for real-time interactive monitoring and evaluation of aircraft tooling in the assembly process
abstract: Aircraft tooling serves as the positioning reference for component assembly, and its real-time displacement monitoring and evaluation are critical to ensuring assembly quality and efficiency. However, existing laser- and vision-based inspection methods struggle to meet the requirements of real-time monitoring due to limited accessibility and low efficiency in confined and occluded assembly environments. To address these pressing engineering needs and current technical limitations, a digital twin-enabled system for real-time interactive monitoring and evaluation of aircraft tooling (DTSAT) in the assembly process is proposed. Based on the proposed DTSAT framework, key enabling methods were developed to achieve ms-level full-field displacement monitoring using only sparse local measurements, while also supporting interactive anomaly alerts throughout the assembly process. In addition, the system integrates a high-performance data storage and retrieval mechanism to ensure full traceability of assembly-related information. A case study on the front spar assembly of an aircraft horizontal tail demonstrates the system’s performance and robustness in monitoring, evaluation, data processing, and traceability, offering a valuable reference for the development of monitoring and evaluation systems under complex manufacturing conditions.

title: CMDF-LSTM-driven feature point identification of CNC G code leveraging geometric and kinematic information
abstract: Identifying feature points in G code is crucial for improving machining accuracy and efficiency in CNC machining. Traditional methods rely on engineers’ experience and predefined geometric thresholds, which commonly fail to account for the actual kinematic and kinetic conditions of the machine tool. This paper proposes a novel, data-driven approach to feature point identification by leveraging both kinematic and geometric information from G code trajectories. A five-phase jerk-limited S-shape interpolation algorithm is employed to generate kinematic characteristics for each point along the trajectory, while three key geometric features are defined to support accurate identification. Building on this, we propose a CNC Machining Data Flow-based Long Short-Term Memory (CMDF-LSTM) model that combines both kinematic and geometric data to automate feature point identification. A training dataset consisting of 12 workpieces and over 105 G code files is generated using Mastercam, with more than 107 setpoints computed through interpolation. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and the real-time feed rate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system further demonstrate the effectiveness. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and quantitative surface roughness measurements at the machined surface further enhance the credibility of experimental conclusions. In addition, the real-time feedrate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system demonstrate the effectiveness from multiple dimensions. This approach provides a scalable and efficient solution for feature point identification in real-world CNC machining applications.

title: Leveraging large language models for smart manufacturing: Reviews, enablers, challenges, and opportunities
abstract: Smart manufacturing is transforming manufacturing landscapes through the integration of advanced information and communication technologies. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized artificial intelligence (AI). However, the application of LLMs in smart manufacturing remains underexplored to address the domain-specific challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and analysis of LLM-enabled smart manufacturing. The latest advancements in LLM for smart manufacturing and the key techniques in LLMs are first reviewed. Subsequently, the key enablers for deploying LLM for smart manufacturing are explored, which include the knowledge graph (KG), agent system, and model context protocol (MCP). Then, the capability across four critical manufacturing domains, including product design, process optimization, predictive maintenance, and remanufacturing are systematically analyzed. Finally, the challenges and opportunities of scaling laws, data privacy and security concerns, the interpretability of LLMs, and the domain-specific knowledge integration within the manufacturing context are also discussed. The outcomes of this research contribute to a responsible and efficient adoption of LLMs, laying a foundation for advancing smart manufacturing practices.

title: Neural–symbolic reasoning for end-of-life product identification in robot-assisted disassembly
abstract: Efficient recycling and reuse of end-of-life products through robot-assisted disassembly has attracted widespread attention in sustainable manufacturing industry. In the robot-assisted disassembly system, the high-precision identification of products and their components is the premise of autonomous disassembly. A series of product identification methods based on deep learning in literature can well identify specific categories of components such as screws. However, different service conditions make products in industrial scenarios highly uncertain in terms of component status, shape and position changes, which make it impossible to predefine categories for products and components, and to obtain high-quality training data sets for new categories in advance. These obstacles make the application of the identification methods to industrial scenarios still challenging. In this paper, a two-stage product identification method based on neural–symbolic reasoning is proposed. In the first stage, deep learning-based methods are used to detect component primitives with limited categories, rather than directly detecting components whose categories cannot be predefined. In the second stage, the logic rules embedded in the word vector space are used to program the detected primitives to infer the semantics of the component to be detected. In addition, a primitive sampling method is proposed to generate new rules by sampling existing rules in the word vector space to improve the generalization of the proposed identification method. The results show a significant increase from 20.01% to 80.89% in successful component identification for the PC product family, along with considerable improvement for others. Code and data are available at http://github.com/nowheresin/neural-symbolic-reasoning-product-identification/.

title: LLM-driven discrete-event simulation: A generative AI framework for automated model generation, adaptation, and evaluation in manufacturing
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) framework for automating the generation, adaptation, and evaluation of discrete-event simulation (DES) models in manufacturing. The approach integrates multiple large language models (LLMs) with a structured blueprint model and targeted human-in-the-loop controls to create executable simulation models from heterogeneous production data, implement targeted modifications, and interpret simulation outcomes. The workflow incorporates prompt engineering, zero- and one-shot implementations, and evaluator–optimizer loops. 21 experimental runs on two industrial case studies from a Swedish automotive manufacturer demonstrate that LLMs can support DES model generation and scenario exploration through a hybrid approach combining automation with human oversight. The results underline both the potential and current limitations of LLM-driven simulation, particularly regarding output consistency and generalizability. Future research should extend the method to more complex manufacturing systems and investigate the role of emerging autonomous Gen-AI tools in simulation-based decision support. • LLM-driven workflow automating discrete-event simulation (DES) model generation, adaptation, and evaluation. • Integrates multiple LLMs with a structured blueprint model and human-in-the-loop oversight. • Systematically tested across 21 runs in two industrial manufacturing case studies. • Demonstrates feasibility for scenario exploration while highlighting challenges in output consistency and reliability.

title: Knowledge-guided multimodal LLM with mixture-of-experts for interpretable defect detection and fault diagnosis: An industrial AI copilot
abstract: The rapid evolution of smart manufacturing has led to an explosion of multimodal data generated from sensors, such as vibration signals, acoustic waves, and surface images. However, traditional learning models often focus on single-modal analysis and lack interpretability, limiting their generalization across different industrial tasks. To address these challenges, this study proposes industrial AI copilot QwIndustry, a multimodal large language model (LLM) designed for industrial tasks, including defect detection and fault diagnosis. The framework integrates a Knowledge-guided Mixture-of-Experts (K-MoE) architecture, which selects different expert neural networks based on the specific industrial task. The parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is adopted to fine-tune Qwen2.5VL, and Chain-of-Thought (COT) distillation to facilitate knowledge-driven multimodal reasoning, enabling the model to achieve reasoning capabilities at a low computational cost. Five diverse industrial datasets involving signal, image, and text modalities were employed to train and evaluate the model. Experimental results show that the proposed QwIndustry with thinking mode achieves superior accuracy over 98% on same-domain tasks and strong cross-domain transferability with accuracy around 95%, maintaining high recognition accuracy on unseen datasets without retraining. Moreover, the model provides human operators with accessible, interpretable reasoning results through natural-language interaction, eliminating the need for deep technical expertise. These results indicate that the Industrial AI Copilot provides an effective and scalable pathway toward knowledge-augmented, human-centric, and interpretable industrial intelligence.

title: An SFDPose network with credible evolution mechanism for digital twin systems in industrial applications
abstract: The rapid rise of Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things (IoT) has elevated digital twins from a novel concept to an indispensable tool for real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization in complex systems. Yet, maintaining the accuracy and reliability of digital twins remains a formidable challenge. As physical entities evolve and operational environments shift, especially in data-driven and resource-constrained contexts, digital twins are prone to degradation, reducing their value and trustworthiness. To address these challenges, in this paper, we introduce a framework that integrates a Separated-Feature Dual-Branch Pose Network (SFDPoseNet) with a credible evolution mechanism. The architecture disentangles and extracts both long-term and short-term features of the twin system in parallel. Specifically, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks capture long-range temporal dependencies, while Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) extract multi-scale local patterns. We propose a lightweight residual Feedforward Neural Network (FFN) that integrates features from dual branches to achieve robust and expressive multivariate time-series forecasting. Complementing this hybrid model, an uncertainty-aware online evolution strategy ensures adaptability. Real-time prediction errors trigger dynamic model updates, while incremental learning with Fisher information–based regularization stabilizes the adaptation process and mitigates catastrophic forgetting. Extensive validation on a quadrotor UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) flight dataset confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art temporal prediction models in both forecasting accuracy and adaptability. Additional ablation studies highlight the distinct contributions of the dual-branch architecture and the evolution mechanism, underscoring the framework’s capability to sustain digital twin reliability under dynamic conditions.

title: Digital twin-based high-precision assembly method for large-diameter cabin section docking
abstract: The docking of the nozzle and combustion chamber is a critical process in the assembly of solid rocket motors. Currently, docking assembly largely relies on manual operations, which constrains production efficiency. To address this, a digital twin-based high-quality assembly method for large-diameter cabin sections is proposed. First, a digital twin model is established using 3D scanning of the physical components. To tackle the challenge of detecting complex 3D assembly features, a feature target-guided digital modeling approach is introduced. By incorporating geometrically marked targets and constructing a digital model with identifiable feature points, the reconstruction of complex feature information is achieved. Subsequently, a collaborative virtual–physical assembly method is developed, employing a multi-camera system for online tracking of the physical components via the digital model. An elliptical cone model is constructed to resolve the misalignment between the center of a perspectively projected ellipse and the actual spatial circle center. The iterative closest point (ICP) based relative pose estimation method is applied to enhance the speed and accuracy of multi-camera vision pose measurement. Finally, a platform was built to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method. Experimental results demonstrate that the digital twin-based assembly approach enables high-efficiency assembly, while also allowing online monitoring and collision warning in visually obscured areas during the process.

title: Twist-pull as an execution skill primitive for robotic disassembly: Safety-aware skill augmentation under contact uncertainty
abstract: Structural variability and hidden contact interactions in robotic disassembly impede conventional task-specific control and learning paradigms. This paper formulates twist-pull (TP) as a fundamental execution skill primitive, a generic interaction pattern underpinning diverse disassembly operations, and proposes a safety-aware skill augmentation framework. Distinct from object-specific policy learning, this approach augments the primitive’s compliant baseline via reinforcement learning (RL) to accommodate unmodeled contact dynamics. To ensure safe exploration, the framework integrates a Safety Policy (SP) for velocity stabilisation and employs a structured observation-action architecture. By explicitly decoupling planar motion regulation from axial compliance modulation, this architectural constraint prevents unsafe force-motion coupling during policy optimisation. Experimental validation across structurally diverse components, spanner-type configurations, and real-world products demonstrates that augmenting the TP primitive significantly enhances execution robustness and generalisability, establishing a scalable foundation for contact-rich disassembly automation. • Twist-Pull is formulated as a generic execution skill primitive for contact-rich disassembly. • A safety-aware framework augments compliant baseline skills via Reinforcement Learning. • Structured network architecture decouples motion and compliance to prevent unsafe coupling. • A dedicated Safety Policy stabilizes velocity modulation during trial-and-error exploration. • The approach generalizes to spanner-mediated operations and diverse industrial products.

title: Digital twin-integrated bandit learning for LRM-driven multi-agent resilient production scheduling
abstract: Industrial systems are moving away from the efficiency-driven mindset of Industry 4.0 towards the more human-focused approach of Industry 5.0, which emphasizes symbiotic manufacturing, resilience, and sustainability. As part of this shift, flexible workshop scheduling needs to continuously adapt and make decisions that are both explainable and responsive to disruptions like fluctuating processing times, equipment failures, and changing order arrivals. This paper highlights the shortcomings of current heuristic methods and introduces a new approach—a Multi-agent, Human–machine Collaborative Resilient Scheduling (MHCRS) system tailored for Industry 5.0. The system uses cognitive digital twins to create a realistic pool of potential disturbances, ensuring consistency between offline learning and real-time operations. Based on this, a Large Reasoning Model (LRM) generates structured and actionable scheduling rules within a defined set of possibilities. A multi-armed bandit mechanism speeds up the process of screening, integrating, and refining rules under conditions with limited data, allowing the rules to evolve smoothly over time while supporting human–machine collaboration and compliance checks. The experiments show that the system, using a process of “LRM generation–Bandit self-evolution–twin evaluation”, can automatically uncover robust rules with better generalization, achieving performance similar to advanced swarm intelligence algorithms. It does so while reducing the time spent searching for solutions by almost ten times, making it highly efficient and practical for real-time rescheduling needs in factory workshops. This work offers a solid framework for scheduling in Industry 5.0, combining resilience, transparency, and continuous evolution.

title: Exploring the core cognitive dynamics of MR-enabled in-situ assembly visualization
Cyber-physical internet-enabled out-of-order execution considering workload for multi-stage scheduling in hybrid flow shop
