title: Handedness-aware motion mapping for human-robot teleoperation via meta-motion alignment and trajectory reconstruction
From artificial intelligence to augmented intelligence: A review of intelligent forward design of wire harnesses
abstract: Flexible wire harnesses serve as the "neural network" and "lifeline" of complex electromechanical systems such as aircraft, ships, and automobiles. Its design flaws directly affect manufacturing feasibility and operational safety, and may even lead to catastrophic failures. Owing to their hybrid rigid-flexible constraints, multidimensional deformations, intricate routing, cross-scale, and high-density integration, flexible harnesses exhibit extremely complex characteristics. These characteristics make the design of a digital mock-up for wire harnesses exceptionally challenging. Achieving effective modeling, simulation, analysis, and optimization of wire harnesses during the design phase—thereby enabling early verification of manufacturing compliance and identification of potential service risks—remains a critical challenge in forward design. This challenge has continuously driven the development of theoretical research mode and methodological framework in the field. However, compared with the well-established theories and mature methodologies of forward design of mechanical system, research on forward design of wire harnesses still has obvious shortcomings. It is therefore urgent to systematically sort out technologies and summarize the development trajectory to accelerate progress in this domain. Therefore, this paper surveys the evolution of forward design methodologies of flexible wire harnesses, with a particular focus on assembly configuration, from an intelligent design perspective. It clarifies research directions, development trends, and research opportunities for intelligent approaches in this field. First, this paper summarizes the forward design paradigm for wire harness characteristics, including multi-scale characteristics, the task framework, and the evolution—from manual, digitalization, artificial intelligence to augmented intelligence. It then reviews the current research status of intelligent forward design research for wire harnesses, emphasizing the application of artificial intelligence techniques such as computer vision, traditional machine learning, deep learning, and metaheuristic algorithms. Afterwards, according to the development requirements of new-generation intelligent manufacturing mode, the study further identifies human-machine collaborative augmented intelligence design—integrating emerging technologies such as mixed reality, generative artificial intelligence, and digital twin—as a key future direction. A prospective research framework for augmented intelligence in forward design of wire harnesses is proposed. On this basis, the paper analyzes key challenges and identifies critical research opportunities in four directions. The developmental trends, future framework, and research opportunities presented herein aim to provide systematic reference and forward-looking guidance for future studies on flexible wire harness, contributing to the ongoing advancement of forward design theory.

title: Planning and evaluation of hybrid manufacturing–remanufacturing systems
abstract: This research presents an approach to plan and evaluate dynamic factory value streams of hybrid manufacturing–remanufacturing systems (HMRS). By considering remanufacturing processes during resource and capacity planning, the proposed model enables the development of factory concepts that allow for better informed decisions regarding material flows as well as lower operational cost. The approach integrates a mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP) for station capacity and material flows planning, with a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) for the dynamic manufacturing–remanufacturing life cycle balancing. For the optimization of the MINLP, a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) is applied. The results of an application use case demonstrate the advantages of the early consideration of remanufacturing into factory planning. The proposed approach enhances manufacturing–remanufacturing systems and demonstrates the benefits of strategic HMRS optimized planning.
keywords: Capacity planning and production concept planning

title: Research on tool wear monitoring based on digital twin and contrastive learning
abstract: Tool wear monitoring system (TWMS)in the machining process can improve production efficiency. The existing TWMS has the characteristics of poor generalization ability of detection model, strong dependence on data, and difficulty in adapting to complex cutting conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes a tool wear monitoring digital twin system (TWM-DTS) using contrastive learning. Firstly, the user interaction and virtual-real linkage are realized through the digital twin system front end (DTS-FE), and the tool state can be perceived in real-time to obtain machining parameters and store them in the buffer. Secondly, this paper proposes a milling force calculation model accounting for tool wear. The digital twin system back end (DTS-BE) can calculate the milling force of different wear conditions in real time through the data of buffer. Finally, this paper proposes a contrastive learning model. By comparing the similarity between the measured milling force (MMF) and the calculated milling force (CMF), the tool wear monitoring under variable working conditions is completed, which provides a judgment basis for the tool change of the digital twin system (DTS) anti-control machine tool. The contrastive model is cross-validated, and the mathematical analysis of the verification results proves that the model has high accuracy and generalization ability. The actual effect of virtual and real combination, tool wear monitoring and system anti-control machine tool change is realized, which lays a foundation for the application of digital twin in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Service composition and optimal selection in cloud remanufacturing considering quality heterogeneity

Coordination of LLM-Embodied Agents for manufacturing task allocation under constraints
abstract: This paper introduces LLM-Embodied Agents (LEAs) for manufacturing task allocation by embedding large language model (LLM) driven cognitive capabilities directly into physical production resources. Despite existing efforts in LLM-based multi-agent coordination, current frameworks do not systematically address the heterogeneous constraints prevalent in manufacturing, particularly task-level spatial constraints. Furthermore, existing frameworks treat automated guided vehicles (AGVs) as passive executors rather than autonomous decision-making agents, leaving their coordination potential unexplored. To address heterogeneous manufacturing constraints, we develop coordination strategies among the LEAs that enable systematic reasoning over capability matching, process precedence relationships, and spatial accessibility requirements. We implement Robot LEAs (RLEAs) and Vehicle LEAs (VLEAs), where robots denote industrial robots and vehicles denote AGVs. We systematically compare two decentralized coordination strategies: Robot-Lead Coordination (RLC), where RLEAs select tasks to process, and Vehicle-Lead Coordination (VLC), where VLEAs recruit machines for task execution. We evaluate the strategies across three manufacturing scenarios with different constraints, including sorting (capability constraints), machining (precedence constraints), and disassembly (spatial and precedence constraints). In disassembly tasks, VLC attains 100% constraint satisfaction versus 63% for RLC using GPT-4o, while reducing total token consumption by 41% and API calls by 68%. Cross-model evaluation with Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and DeepSeek-R1 confirms VLC’s robustness across different LLM backbones, while ablation studies demonstrate that failure memory significantly improves RLC performance but provides marginal gains for VLC. Scalability analysis shows VLC scales at a substantially lower rate than RLC as problem size increases.

title: AGV scheduling in shopfloor logistics of semiconductor assembly
abstract: Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) are integral to indoor logistics, especially in uncertain manufacturing settings, such as semiconductor fabrication and automated warehouses. Traditional AGV dispatching strategies aim at transportation efficiency, but they overlook problem structure stemming from production process characteristics. This paper introduces a new family of logistical task scheduling algorithms that considers production phases. We propose a set of AGV dispatching strategies and low-latency scheduling heuristics. Specifically, we present a so-called bucketing scheme that groups logistical tasks based on their association with a production phase and facility layout. Through detailed simulations, we demonstrate that phase-aware scheduling significantly increases throughput, while no single strategy is ideal across all scenarios. Bucketing also becomes a practical replacement for predictive models in fitting environments. Our findings present a comprehensive scheduling framework for shopfloor logistics that captures real-time requirements of production and provides an optimization approach with reasonable computational effort.

title: Mapping technological advances in drilling for aircraft manufacturing: A hybrid bibliometric and expert-guided review
Machine learning-driven digital twin for real-time temperature prediction and adaptive process control in large-scale additive manufacturing
abstract: Temperature management in large-scale additive manufacturing (LSAM) plays an important role in interlayer bonding strength and print quality. This study develops a digital twin which predicts the real-time temperature and provides adaptive control of printing parameters in robotic LSAM of polymer structures. A finite-difference model was developed to simulate the thermal behavior under various print velocities, feed rates, and specimen dimensions and the results were validated against experimental temperature measurements using a thermal camera. Simulation data were used to train a machine learning model to predict the temperature of the newly deposited layer in real time based on input data of print geometry and process parameters. It was demonstrated how geometry and printing parameters can significantly impact interlayer temperature and, consequently, the overall printing quality and the interlayer bonding strength through experiments. Another machine learning model is trained to predict printing process parameters such as print speed and feeding rate based on the user input parameters (e.g. print geometrical parameters, etc.) to achieve the desired print quality. A digital twin is developed integrating the joint data from the robotic system to visualize the extruder trajectory, predict the temperature distribution of the newly deposited layer in real time as well as to adaptively control the printing process parameters during the printing process to achieve the proper interlayer temperature and desired print quality. The developed digital framework provides a foundation for real-time LSAM process monitoring, control and adjustment, offering new capabilities for improving print quality and minimizing defects in real time. • Finite-difference thermal model for LSAM validated against experiments with 5% error • Interlayer temperature strongly influences interlayer bonding and print quality. • ML model was developed for real-time temperature prediction in digital twin. • Data-driven digital twin enables real-time temperature vision and adaptive control. • Digital twin achieves desired interlayer temperature and raster width.

title: A STEP-NC-based post-process simulation system for closed-loop machining
Active learning using hybrid surrogate tool life modeling for machining process optimization
abstract: This paper describes an active learning approach for part-to-part iterative machining process optimization using a hybrid surrogate tool life model. A probabilistic interpolating tool life model is developed by combining the empirical Taylor-type tool life equation and the model fit error. The probabilistic tool life model is then used to calculate the machining cost per part distribution. The optimal machining parameters are selected using an expected improvement in machining cost per part criterion. The method is validated numerically using experimental results; the results show a median convergence error of 2.2% after three tests over 400 simulations. The method is validated experimentally on two industrial applications for Ti-6Al-4V roughing resulting in a cost per part reduction greater than 23% after two tests. The described method is a robust solution for rapid convergence to optimal machining parameters in an industrial production environment.

title: Editorial Board
Dual-stream adaptive graph convolutional network with enhanced skeleton representation for human-robot collaborative assembly intention recognition
abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA), which combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, has become a core paradigm for smart manufacturing in Industry 5.0. Dynamic action intention recognition is a key technology for seamless human-robot interaction. However, the complexity of industrial assembly scenarios makes it difficult for collaborative robots to accurately understand the operator's assembly action intentions. Most existing methods rely on graph convolutional networks with fixed skeletal topologies, lacking the capability to capture cross-joint dependencies tailored to different action samples. These approaches depend on a single type of human skeletal feature (e.g., joint coordinates) and fail to effectively integrate multi-level dynamic information (e.g., joint trajectory kinematics and bone-level geometric transformations), resulting in an incomplete semantic representation of human action intention. To address these issues, this paper proposes an HRCA action intention recognition method based on a Dual-stream Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (DS-AGCN) model. Firstly, a simplified human skeletal structure is designed by removing redundant joints irrelevant to assembly actions, making it more suitable for recognizing upper-body movements in HRCA scenarios. Secondly, to enhance the model's generalization capability against operators’ individual differences, six data augmentation strategies are introduced. Then, an adaptive adjacency matrix is incorporated into the proposed method to strengthen the learning of dynamic dependencies between human joints that are not naturally connected. Finally, a dual-stream feature fusion mechanism is proposed. By embedding a motion stream within the joint stream, the operator's assembly actions are characterized from two dimensions: raw joint coordinates and joint motion features, thereby improving the accuracy of HRCA intention recognition. In the experiment, a HRCA experimental platform for a cylinder gear reducer is designed and developed, and an HRCA action video dataset is constructed based on it. The proposed method is experimentally validated using this dataset. The experimental results, including the model's training convergence performance, the enhancement effect of data augmentation strategies and adaptive adjacency matrix, and visualizations of the learning process across different network layers, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with eight other state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method achieves the best performance on four evaluation metrics, with an Accuracy of 96.97%, Precision of 97.08%, Recall of 96.97%, and F1-score of 96.95%, demonstrating its superiority in the recognition accuracy for HRCA intention.

title: Advances of large language models for smart manufacturing
Dynamic coordinated decision-making for integrated production and transportation in reconfigurable manufacturing systems via edge-enhanced heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning
abstract: Reconfigurable manufacturing systems (RMSs) utilize reconfigurable machine tools and flexible material handling systems to enhance adaptability and responsiveness, supporting growing demand for mass customization. Nevertheless, tight coupling among production, transportation, and reconfiguration decisions in dynamic environments makes system-level coordinated decision-making highly challenging. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches, constrained by inadequate state representations, fail to capture the heterogeneous and tightly coupled interactions inherent in RMS operations. To address this challenge, we propose an edge-enhanced heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning approach (EHGRL) for the dynamic coordination of integrated production and transportation in RMSs. The problem is formulated as a Markov decision process, where system states are represented by an integrated reconfiguration-transportation disjunctive graph that explicitly encodes heterogeneous entities and their interactions. An edge-enhanced tri-relational heterogeneous attention network is further developed to embed the graph by incorporating edge-enhanced attention with multi-level node-edge-semantic information fusion, enabling expressive state representations and effective end-to-end decisions. Extensive experiments on 760 instances demonstrate that EHGRL outperforms the compared methods, achieving up to 75.1% and 71.5% average relative percentage deviation reductions relative to the best baseline in comparative and generalization studies, respectively, while maintaining millisecond-level online inference, highlighting its robustness, generalization capability, and deployment potential in complex RMS environments.

title: A new explainable artificial intelligence algorithm integrated with multi-agent system for joint decision-making of smart manufacturing systems
abstract: Smart manufacturing systems increasingly rely on integrated production, inspection, and maintenance decisions to achieve high economic performance while satisfying stringent quality and reliability constraints under nonstationary operating conditions. Fixed inspection thresholds and periodic maintenance schedules often fail to adapt to evolving equipment states, leading to infeasible operation and suboptimal profit. This paper proposes a new Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based Multi-Agent System (MAS) decision-making algorithm for quality-critical smart manufacturing systems, addressing production, inspection, and maintenance decisions within a unified framework. A data-driven wear proxy triggers condition-based maintenance, while XAI fidelity signals dynamically adjust both inspection thresholds and effective maintenance wear thresholds when explanation fidelity indicates unreliable predictions. Global feasibility with respect to false-positive and false-negative constraints is enforced through an augmented Lagrangian optimization that supports policy parameters over long horizons. Case studies using large-scale industrial data demonstrate that the proposed MAS-XAI policy significantly outperforms both periodic maintenance strategies and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy. Relative to DQN, MAS-XAI achieves a 14.28% profit increase. Compared with periodic maintenance, it reduces maintenance interventions by 55.2% while maintaining a strict false-negative rate of 0.82%. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves operational robustness and economic performance in smart manufacturing systems under dynamic conditions.
keywords: Integrated Production and Maintenance Decision Making

title: A novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model
abstract: In the autonomy problem of large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing orders, three steps are usually involved: allocating orders among enterprises, assigning parts to 3D printers, and arranging parts on the printer’s build platform. Among these steps, the layout of parts on a 3D printer serves as the underlying layer of the autonomy loop, providing the basis for obtaining feedback during part-equipment matching and enabling real-time adjustments. It also affects the allocation of orders among enterprises. Currently, artificial intelligence (AI) agents specifically designed for part layout remain underdeveloped, and practical engineering applications still rely heavily on manual operations. Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model (SPVLM), aiming to provide an effective AI agent solution for the autonomous parts layout stage. We propose an autonomy architecture for large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing. For the part layout problem in 3D printing, we propose a visual-text evidence enhancement method and construct a dataset of 10,000 scene samples. We further propose an improved generative reinforcement policy optimization (GRPO) technique to enhance the layout decision-making capability of SPVLMs. Finally, based on the SPVLM, we build an AI agent using a reasoning and acting (ReAct) architecture. The AI agent continually acquires part-layout experience through a memory-augmentation strategy and supports lightweight deployment. A representative subset of the dataset is made publicly available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RTYGFb2dvBAsXXD5v7OTXq07QpIXMcTA?usp=drive_link

title: Unit-oriented aeroengine assembly and test-run linkage framework: A data-driven complex network approach
abstract: The performance of aeroengines, as complex and precise thermodynamic systems, is highly influenced by assembly quality. However, the lack of integration between assembly and test-run stages hampers the effective use of massive assembly data for closed-loop optimization. Moreover, in mass production characterized by unit-oriented structural design, there is no scalable method to pre-evaluate unit assembly quality. These limitations lead to greater variability in full-machine performance and higher test-run failure rates, which causes rework and significantly increases manufacturing costs. To address this, a unit-oriented aeroengine assembly and test-run linkage framework is proposed. Firstly, assembly data are used to construct network and dynamics models to characterize unit assembly quality. Combined with resilience theory, the unit assembly quality evaluation index and qualified interval are proposed, enabling pre-evaluation and filtering of units before full-machine assembly. Next, using Bayesian theory, the unit-oriented full-machine test-run performance prediction model is constructed, capturing the causal links and probability mappings between unit combinations and full-machine performance. Finally, integrating the above models, the current assembly and test-run process is optimized by building a qualified unit library, predicting the full-machine test-run pass probability of unit combinations, and using feedback from test results to generate actionable assembly recommendations, thereby achieving coordination between assembly and testing. According to the experimental results, the dynamic model achieves fitting errors as low as 2%, underscoring its high accuracy and reliability in characterizing unit assembly quality, while the test-run results and maintenance records provide strong empirical validation. This framework improves coordination between assembly and test-run processes, reduces failure and rework, and supports unit interchangeability and optimal matching. It also underpins the development of digital engineering and intelligent assembly, with significant engineering value and broad application prospects.

title: Perception, assessment and enhancement for operators in human-centric manufacturing cells: An ergonomics-oriented systematic review
Bridging 2D vision and 3D CAD: Integrating cross-modal deep learning and LLM-assisted semantic graph reasoning for spatial disassembly constraint modelling
abstract: To advance automation in the remanufacturing sector, this paper proposes a novel spatial disassembly constraint modelling method that integrates cross-modal deep learning with the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). A significant challenge in robotic disassembly is accurately identifying spatial constraints for used products, which often exhibit uncertain conditions and structural deviations from original designs. To address this, we introduce a cross-modal deep learning technique that unifies the detection mechanism for both captured images of used products and CAD models of original products, effectively resolving multimodal data fusion issues during model training. Furthermore, we leverage LLMs to construct and match semantic graphs based on the spatial positional relationships among components. This allows for the precise identification of the optimal matching CAD model and the correct numbering of detected components, thereby deriving specific spatial constraints for each component. The rigour and performance of this method are validated through a case study involving the removal of used bolster springs from railway wagon bogies on a robotic platform. The results demonstrate that the proposed method enables robots to accurately construct spatial disassembly constraints under complex and uncertain conditions, facilitating automated disassembly operations.

Embodied intelligent industrial robotics: Framework and techniques
abstract: The combination of embodied intelligence and robots has great prospects and is becoming increasingly common. In order to work more efficiently, accurately, reliably, and safely in industrial scenarios, robots should have at least general knowledge, working-environment knowledge, and operating-object knowledge. These pose significant challenges to existing embodied intelligent robotics (EIR) techniques. Thus, this paper first briefly reviews the history of industrial robotics and analyzes the limitations of mainstream EIR frameworks. Then, a new knowledge-driven technical framework of embodied intelligent industrial robotics (EIIR) is proposed for various industrial environments. It has five modules: a world model, a high-level task planner, a low-level skill controller, a simulator, and a physical system. The development of techniques related to each module are also thoroughly reviewed, and recent progress regarding their adaption to industrial applications are discussed. A case study of real-world assembly system is given to demonstrate the newly proposed EIIR framework's applicability and potentiality. Finally, the key challenges that EIIR encounters in industrial scenarios are summarized and future research directions are suggested. The authors believe that EIIR technology is shaping the next generation of industrial robotics and EIIR-based industrial systems supply a new technological paradigm for intelligent manufacturing. It is expected that this review could serve as a valuable reference for scholars and engineers that are interested in industrial embodied intelligence. Together, scholars can use this research to drive their rapid advancement and application of EIIR techniques. The authors would continue to track and contribute new studies in the project page https://github.com/jackyzengl/EIIR

Distributionally Robust Asynchronous Federated Learning for Anomaly Detection in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) additive manufacturing involves low-volume, highly flexible part designs that generate heterogeneous process data. When equipped with in-situ sensors, these systems produce massive volumes of high-dimensional data, creating significant challenges for real-time quality monitoring. This paper proposes a Distributionally Robust Asynchronous Federated Learning (DRO-AFL) framework for collaborative thermal process anomaly detection across multiple L-PBF operations without sharing sensitive process data. The framework integrates three key components: (1) asynchronous federated learning with convolutional autoencoders for flexible client participation; (2) multilinear principal component analysis for efficient dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional tensor data; and (3) distributionally robust optimization for improved model generalization across heterogeneous data distributions. Unlike conventional synchronous federated learning, DRO-AFL accommodates immediate updates from available clients without waiting for stragglers, making it well-suited to manufacturing environments with diverse computational resources. Trained using real L-PBF thermal imaging data, DRO-AFL achieves comparable reconstruction accuracy to FedAvg, centralized, and individual learning baselines and demonstrates improved spatio-temporal anomaly detection capability through a hybrid scoring approach. The results highlight DRO-AFL as a robust approach for thermal anomaly detection in distributed manufacturing systems.

title: Carbon-aware scheduling via adaptive large neighborhood search with destroy–repair mechanisms for integrated maintenance planning on parallel machines
Architectures of biointelligent value creation systems: A systematic literature review and typology
abstract: Biointelligent value creation systems (BVS) impose a structural design tension: distributed multi-actor production across heterogeneous networks must coexist with enforceable cross-actor governance, biological variability management, and auditable compliance documentation at every actor interface. Conventional value creation architectures (VCAs) typically address either production distribution or governance depth, not both simultaneously. No consolidated typology exists that assesses which architectures can sustain this combination under domain-specific BVS coordination requirements. This paper addresses that gap through a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of 40 publications, synthesized via qualitative content analysis into ten VCA archetypes across four coordination logics: vertical/boundary architectures, platform and ecosystem architectures, modular and service architectures, and circular loop architectures. Validation searches confirmed completeness and extended the evidence base to 48. Each archetype was assessed for BVS suitability using a 6 C + SET profiling framework applied against a seven-dimensional BVS characteristics model established in companion work. Four archetypes are structurally suitable as standalone BVS coordination mechanisms: role-based orchestration, ecosystem coordination, service-led logistics integration, and circular loop governance. Four further archetypes are conditionally suitable. They contain the structural premises but degrade predictably without specific governance investment. Two archetypes operate through transactional coordination logic and cannot reach the governance depth required for compliant multi-actor biological production. Suitable archetypes share three structural features: explicit role differentiation with enforceable accountability, auditable interface obligations, and governance regimes that sustain compliance under biological variability. The resulting typology provides a traceable, domain-specific architecture map for BVS and serves as the basis for archetype-dependent design guidelines for information logistics systems in BVS settings.

title: MET-Net: An equivalent-section mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning in bilayer tube springback prediction under data scarcity and incomplete physical mechanisms
abstract: Industry 4.0 requires transparent and reliable prediction of manufacturing outcomes, which is often constrained by scarce data and incomplete physical mechanisms. These constraints are particularly severe for bent bilayer metal tubes, whose springback prediction is essential for process planning. This work proposes MET-Net, a mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning that reuses abundant single-layer springback knowledge for data-scarce bilayer prediction. MET-Net maps bilayer cross-section parameters to an equivalent single-layer representation through a differentiable equivalent-section module, whose adaptation is restricted to two physically meaningful correction parameters. The model is trained in two stages: physics-based initialization and single-layer pretraining, followed by conservative bilayer fine-tuning with sparse physics-residual guardrails, and a lightweight affine calibrator. On a copper-aluminum rotary draw bending case, MET-Net achieves a median RMSE of 0.4835° using only 100 bilayer samples, approaching the accuracy of a single-layer baseline trained on ten times more data. A paired zero-shot environment-perturbation evaluation further indicates stable performance under environment-level perturbations. Beyond accuracy, MET-Net supports manufacturing transparency through a structurally interpretable mechanism pathway, DeepLIFT-based training monitoring, and post-hoc diagnosability analyses. These strategies identify validity regimes of the embedded equivalent-section theory and quantify where systematic correction is required. MET-Net therefore provides accurate bilayer springback prediction together with actionable mechanism insight for process planning under data scarcity and incomplete physics.

title: Granger causality-guided dynamic multiobjective operation optimization for batch polymerization process
Proactive energy-carbon aware production scheduling in SMT lines: A novel graph meta-reinforcement learning approach
abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing requires Surface Mount Technology (SMT) lines to adopt energy-carbon aware production scheduling. Traditional paradigms treat machines as discrete states, failing to capture the continuous thermodynamic inertia of thermal equipment like reflow ovens. Coupled with dynamic electricity prices and fluctuating carbon factors, classical optimization and standard multi-agent reinforcement learning become inadequate. To address the deep coupling of discrete manufacturing logic and continuous thermodynamics, we reformulate the scheduling problem as a semi-Markov decision process and propose a novel graph meta-reinforcement learning architecture termed GMeta-MATD3. Specifically, graph neural networks are utilized to extract spatial–temporal topologies across production and microgrid networks. To navigate environmental non-stationarity, a meta-learning module is embedded within each agent to infer latent physical contexts and predict peer behaviors, enabling temporal energy arbitrage via deliberate “wait” actions. Additionally, an attention-based centralized critic dynamically decomposes joint values to resolve the multi-agent credit assignment problem. Extensive experiments on real SMT data coupled with IEEE distribution systems demonstrate significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. GMeta-MATD3 achieves the best Pareto front, yielding a 13.1h makespan, 1020.5 RMB energy cost, 810.2 kgCO2 emissions, a 1.5% tardiness rate, and zero grid violations. Crucially, its thermodynamic stepping mechanism reduces transition energy from 12.5 to 3.2 kWh/batch, and proactive peak avoidance cuts the load peak-to-valley difference by 34.5%, maintaining daily carbon intensity below 0.55 kgCO2/kWh. Scalability tests confirm that executing 500-batch schedules in under 500 ms.

title: A comprehensive review of robotic assembly of aerospace components
Towards semi-supervised and unsupervised source verification of additively manufactured parts with sparse data
abstract: A common challenge for manufacturing supply chains is to determine whether parts were made correctly, using the intended machines and processes. This study presents a deep learning framework that can discover and verify the source of additively manufactured (AM) components from surface texture visible in part images, with minimal pre-training or supervision. We develop a machine learning (ML) architecture that integrates self-supervised feature extraction using a vision transformer masked autoencoder (ViT-MAE) with unsupervised Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering. A simple classification head guides feature extraction when labels are available. To evaluate the model performance, we procured 3744 AM parts from six contract manufacturers. These manufacturers produced the parts using a total of 11 Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printers. Part images were used to evaluate the model across various unsupervised and semi-supervised tasks for predicting manufacturing origin. With no part labels, the model achieves an F1 score of 0.595 identifying the specific printer that produced the part. With minimally labeled data, only 36 parts from a single build per printer, the F1 score exceeds 0.9, outperforming existing supervised models. The architecture identifies anomalous parts from unknown sources in complex recognition tasks, including Open Set Recognition (OSR) and Generalized Category Discovery (GCD). The model identifies other fine-grained manufacturing attributes including the printer model, material, specific build, and location of the part in the printer. The research presents an image-based deep learning method that could enable manufacturers to validate parts from suppliers in data-scarce environments.

title: Optimizing contact-guided search for robotic screw unfastening under position uncertainty in electronic waste dismantling
abstract: Automating the disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) is crucial for the circular economy and the recovery of strategic materials like Rare Earth Elements. However, autonomous fastener removal remains a significant bottleneck due to the high positional uncertainty and degradation inherent in End-of-Life (EoL) products. This research proposes a deterministic, geometry-adaptable framework that integrates deep learning-based vision for coarse localization with a Hybrid Force/Velocity Control (HFVC) architecture for robust unscrewing. Five search geometries, including the Circular Spiral, Square Spiral, Windmill Search, Raster Scan, and Spiral with Noise, are compared in simulation, identifying the first of these as the most optimal strategy for industrial applications. Unlike empirical methods, we mathematically derive the kinematic constraints — specifically the maximum allowable spiral pitch and the optimal rotational velocity windows — required to guarantee successful insertion without heuristic tuning. Experimental validation using an industrial manipulator demonstrates the framework’s scalability across four distinct drive profiles (Allen, Hexagonal, Torx, and Phillips) without any parameter readjustment. The system successfully absorbs initial positional errors of up to 3 mm, achieving an overall 99% success rate with cycle times ranging from 11 to 13 s/screw depending on the fastener type, proving highly competitive for high-throughput automated dismantling lines.

title: Multi-view fusion for human action recognition and cognitive assistive systems in industrial assembly
XR-based training for technical skills in manufacturing
abstract: Manufacturing systems are undergoing rapid transformation driven by global, economic, and sustainability pressures, increasing the need for scalable training solutions to support technical skill development and faster industrialization. However, conventional training methods for manual operations often rely on material-intensive trial-and-error, resulting in material waste, long onboarding times, and dependence on expert supervision. While Extended Reality (XR) has shown strong potential for cognitive and procedural training, its effectiveness for technical, motor-skill–based tasks remain debated due to limited physical interaction, haptic realism, and support for precise tool handling. This study addresses this gap by investigating the use of Mixed Reality (MR) for early-stage technical skill training in manual sealant application within an automotive manufacturing context. An MR training system was developed, integrating physical tools and props to preserve eye-to-hand coordination and interaction fidelity. A lab experiment evaluating tool-tracking accuracy against robotic ground truth data showed an average deviation of 7.7 mm, indicating sufficient precision for early-stage technical skill development when compared to domain specific thresholds. Furthermore, an on-site user study with 45 professional sealant operators assessed usability and acceptance. The results demonstrate high usability and strong user acceptance, with operators reporting increased confidence and reduced reliance on traditional training materials. Additionally, the MR system enabled faster training iterations while reducing material waste and setup time. These findings suggest that XR-based training can effectively support early-stage technical skill development. While evaluated in an automotive sealant application, the approach shows potential for broader applicability to manufacturing tasks requiring tool handling and motor-skills.

title: Facilitating digital assembly: A physics-informed graph learning framework for prediction of assembly deviations in bolted flange connections
abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity prediction of assembly deviations is critical for the digital assembly of high-precision products. In the assembly of bolted flange connections, bolt preload induces micro-scale deformations that are intrinsically coupled with complex contact mechanics. However, resolving these deformations via Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is computationally intensive, while purely data-driven models often lack physical consistency and generalization robustness. To address this, we propose a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PI-GNN) framework for rapid displacement field prediction. This architecture explicitly encodes the topological dependencies of unstructured meshes via graph learning while embedding Navier–Cauchy equilibrium residuals into the loss function to enforce physical validity. Crucially, to address the sharp stress gradients inherent in contact surface, a distance-weighted supervision mechanism is introduced to stabilize training on sparse datasets. Comprehensive benchmarks on L-block assemblies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves simulation-grade fidelity with minimal data dependence. Compared to the purely data-driven baseline, the PI-GNN exhibits superior extrapolation robustness, reducing the axial Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by up to 48.8% in OOD regimes. Finally, the method is applied to the assembly deviation prediction of a two-stage flange connection. Experimental validation focusing on physical end-face tilt measurements confirms the model’s ability to accurately characterize macroscopic assembly posture variations, verifying its potential as a reliable framework for intelligent assembly and in-process quality monitoring.

title: An interpretable data-model fusion method for thermal error prediction of motorized spindle of CNC machine tools
Machine learning-aided material selection, parameter optimization, and process monitoring in laser powder bed fusion and laser directed energy deposition with powder feed
abstract: Laser-based metal additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, such as laser powder bed fusion and laserbased directed energy deposition, have been broadly adopted in a wide range of industries, including the aerospace, automotive, biomedical, and energy sectors. These technologies require cross-scale coordination spanning six orders of magnitude, involving complex interactions between laser parameters, feedstock properties, and thermal-fluid dynamics. The resulting high-dimensional datasets span materials, processing parameters, laser-metal interaction, and final part properties, posing significant challenges to understanding intricate processing-structure-property (P-S-P) relationships. Recent advances in machine learning (ML), with its capacity to uncover hidden patterns and correlations from large, high-dimensional datasets, present a transformative approach to accelerate discovery and optimization in metal AM. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances and challenges in employing various ML methods across key stages of the metal AM workflow. We explore the application of ML in the following aspects: (1) The ML-aided selection of materials, covering new materials development and metal powder selection; (2) The ML-aided optimization of processing parameters, including the establishment of processing maps and the implementation of optimization strategies; (3) The ML-aided in situ monitoring and quality assurance of the AM processes using sensors, including acoustic emission, visible light, infrared, synchrotron X-ray, and multi-sensor systems. Moreover, we examine the characteristics, limitations, and data requirements of various ML models in each of these domains, guiding model selection and experimental design. By adopting an ML-centric perspective, this review aims to inform future research directions, support the development of more autonomous metal AM systems, and accelerate the optimization of laser-based metal AM.

title: Probabilistic Mixture of Experts framework for real-time multi-anomaly detection in smart manufacturing systems
abstract: Real-time multi-anomaly detection in smart manufacturing faces significant challenges due to process heterogeneity, temporal variability, and the scarcity of instance-level labeling. This paper introduces a novel probabilistic Mixture of Experts (MoE) framework that utilizes unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) experts to capture class-specific dynamics without requiring precise instance-level labels during training. The framework employs a hard-gating probabilistic rule for real-time instance-level monitoring and a signal-level decision aggregation scheme to ensure consistent process-cycle classification. Validated on a 30-hour continuous rocket assembly dataset from the Future Factories laboratory, the proposed MoE approach achieves high-accuracy discrimination across multiple defect classes, significantly outperforming conventional baselines. The model’s deployment capability is further demonstrated in a virtual Testbed-as-a-Service (TaaS) environment, showcasing its suitability for lightweight, real-time industrial monitoring. This study offers a scalable and interpretable solution for intelligent manufacturing systems dealing with data sparsity, heterogeneity, weak label supervision constraints, and complex multi-anomaly scenarios.

title: Physics-informed machine learning for intelligent process monitoring: A sensorless approach for cutting force estimation based on feed drive dynamics and motor current
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for estimating cutting forces in CNC machining by integrating feed drive dynamics and motor current signals with machine learning (ML) algorithms. The methodology leverages the mechanical behavior of feed drive components, modeling the interactions among servomotors, leadscrews, and other elements to analytically estimate cutting forces, incorporating a Stribeck friction model to accurately represent frictional losses. By utilizing data directly from CNC controllers, the proposed method offers a practical and scalable solution for in-process force monitoring, without the need for external sensors or costly instrumentation. To enhance prediction accuracy, a hybrid Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) framework based on physics-based feature augmentation was developed combining analytically estimated forces based on feed drive model with servo signals and machining parameters. This framework not only improves the accuracy of the analytical model but also reduces the need for extensive experimentation used in direct data driven approaches. The results highlight the effectiveness of this approach, with R² values exceeding 98% and significantly reduced root mean square error (RMSE) values. Notably, the proposed PIML framework achieved an improvement of approximately 28–32% in prediction accuracy compared to the standalone analytical model, and 15–22% over conventional ML models that rely solely on data-driven inference. This integration not only captures nonlinearities and dynamic behavior but also retains the interpretability of the analytical model. The findings underline the added value of incorporating domain knowledge into ML algorithms, enabling more reliable force estimation directly from CNC controller data. Furthermore, the model demonstrated strong generalization capabilities when tested on unseen data, reinforcing its applicability in real-world manufacturing environments.

title: A sustainable mass individualization paradigm of high-entropy manufacturing systems towards Industry 5.0: retrospect and prospect
Accelerating life cycle inventory development through correlation-aware multi-fidelity transfer learning: Case studies in cradle-to-gate manufacturing energy modeling
abstract: Accurate, parametric cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) models of production systems are essential for environmentally motivated process comparison and optimization; however, commercially-available Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) databases are often too inaccurate for confident decision-making, while more accurate process and/or site-specific data-driven modeling can require prohibitively expensive experimental campaigns. In this work, a multi-fidelity transfer learning (MFTL) framework is developed for cradle-to-gate LCA that combines a low-fidelity reduced-order model, embedding basic physics or experience as a principled head start, with a high-fidelity adaptive boosting mechanism based on limited experimental data. The framework accelerates learning and helps prevent overfitting by augmenting the traditional residual-based loss with a correlation-aware term. The framework is demonstrated by modeling energy-related inventory data in two manufacturing processes: roller power consumption in aluminum cold rolling and energy use in polymer extrusion-based additive manufacturing (AM). The correlation-aware MFTL framework achieved R 2 validation scores of 0.99 and 0.98 using just 60% and 12% of the data collected from experiments on the rolling and AM case studies, respectively. This predictive accuracy outperformed Traditional MFTL ( R 2 validation scores of 0.88 and 0.83) and purely data-driven approaches such as a neural network and a support vector regressor ( R 2 validation scores of 0.85 and 0.84) when trained on the same amount of data. Overall, the framework enables accelerated, accurate, parametric modeling of LCI data, supporting the development of sustainable manufacturing systems.

title: Knowledge graph-enhanced evolutionary multitasking matheuristic algorithm for job shop scheduling problem with discrete operation sequence flexibility
CoLMAgent: A collaborative agentic AI system that integrates large and small models for industrial intelligent human–machine interactions
abstract: With the advent of the Industrial 5.0 era, scenarios such as intelligent manufacturing and equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) have increased the requirements for high-quality human–machine interaction. Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in terms of semantic understanding and generation for industrial question answering, fault diagnosis, and intelligent O&M, they face challenges such as hallucination and a high computational cost. To address these issues, CoLMAgent, a collaborative agentic AI system that integrates large and small models for industrial intelligent human–machine interactions, is proposed. First, a semantic structuring model (SSM) is constructed to parse users’ unstructured natural language into a domain-specific structured semantic representation. Second, we propose a process agent model (PAM) paradigm that modularly orchestrates small models according to the process workflows to form executable task-specific processes. Third, a collaborative matching mechanism for large–small models based on multidimensional evaluation is designed to select the agent that best meets the process–agent user requirements; moreover, prompt templates are used to inject the agents’ computed results into the LLM generation process, thereby improving the professionalism of industrial human–machine interactions. Experimental results on a Chinese intelligent O&M question-answering dataset from real engineering scenarios indicate that CoLMAgent outperforms the baseline models in terms of the BERTScore, RQUGE and BARTScore, thus showing that it achieves high-quality content generation for industrial human–machine interactions.

title: A graph isomorphism attention network and graph information embedded reinforcement learning-based dual-arm robot teleoperation and manipulation skill acquisition method
abstract: Many human working environments are arduous, and entirely replacing on-site workers with robots remains challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a teleoperation and manipulation skill learning framework for physical avatar robots. For teleoperation, a real-time, dual-arm motion retargeting method based on a graph isomorphism attention network (GIAN) and robust kalman filtering (RKF) has been developed. This method eliminates the need for manually labeled human-to-robot joint mappings. By representing human motion as graph-structured data and leveraging a learning approach with kinematic physical constraints, accurate retargeting is achieved. The RKF is adopted to suppresses noise and outliers for enhancing stability. For skill learning, the study introduces a graph information-embedded reinforcement learning (GIERL) method that integrates imitation and reinforcement learning. Graph features extracted by GIAN are incorporated into both the observation space and reward design, enabling efficient acquisition of dual-arm manipulation skills. Furthermore, a shared control strategy is designed by integrating GIERL with GIAN to augment manipulation, forming a synergistic closed loop between perception and decision-making. Experiments involving desktop organization, as well as dual-arm box lifting and transportation in both simulated and real environments, demonstrate the superior performance and practicality of the proposed framework.

title: KG-CoPlan: A knowledge-grounded and H-FSM driven large-small model collaborative framework for generative manufacturing process planning in industry 5.0
Human–robot collaborative disassembly line balancing with ergonomic awareness for scalable circular production
Vision language model-enhanced embodied intelligence for AR-assisted HRC assembly: Multimodal cognition, task reasoning, and autonomous execution
abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly is pivotal to modern manufacturing, yet it suffers from critical bottlenecks that hinder its performance. The fusion of visual, textual, and operational multimodal information remains inefficient, and human-robot task partitioning is often ambiguous. This ambiguity arises from inadequate integration of domain knowledge with perceptual outputs, while manual assembly operations lack consistency and a notable disjunction exists between abstract task reasoning and embodied robotic execution. These issues collectively impede the intelligence and coordination of HRC assembly systems. To resolve these issues, this study proposes an end-to-end Vision-Language Model (VLM)-enhanced embodied intelligent framework for HRC assembly’s cognitive reasoning and autonomous execution. The framework adopts a closed-loop architecture with four cascaded core modules, synergistically supporting perception, knowledge reasoning, human-robot interaction, and autonomous execution. First, a VLM-driven multimodal cognition module innovatively fuses VLMs with BERT (textual semantic processing) and ResNet-50 (visual feature extraction), capturing fine-grained features of assembly personnel, parts and tools to generate structured perceptual representations via semantic triplets and state matrices. Second, a domain knowledge-driven reasoning module is developed, which constructs an assembly knowledge graph by extracting semantic triplets from corpora via VLMs and encodes domain experience into machine-readable form. It adopts Graph RAG for semantic alignment, conflict detection and structured retrieval, and leverages LLM-aided reasoning to decompose global tasks into robotic and manual subtasks with clear boundaries. Third, an AR-assisted assembly guidance module is proposed to enable seamless HRC interaction and precise manual operations through multi-dimensional guidance. It covers visual-textual prompts, 3D positioning overlays, real-time monitoring and remote consultation, translating reasoned manual subtasks into actionable guidelines. Finally, a VLM-driven robotic code generation module realizes autonomous execution by generating modular action functions, sequences and trajectory parameters based on reasoned task representations. Integrated with hardware components, it uses an embodied controller to convert abstract robotic subtasks into concrete physical operations. Comparative experiments with traditional models and LLMs confirm the proposed HRC assembly system’s superiority.

title: Human-robot collaborative assembly towards human-centric manufacturing paradigm: a review
Adaptive parameter optimization for turbine blade manufacturing: A novel personalized federated learning framework
abstract: In high-precision machining processes such as turbine blade manufacturing, optimizing process parameters is crucial for improving production efficiency and precision. However, process parameter optimization in current industrial practice still suffers from two major drawbacks: the slow convergence speed of high-dimensional parameter optimization and the protection of manufacturing data privacy. To address these issues, this article proposes a Sophia Extended (SophiaX) optimization algorithm under the novel personalized federated learning (DecePFL) framework. Specifically, the SophiaX algorithm is proposed, which efficiently utilizes second-order information through adaptive estimates of diagonal Hessian, significantly accelerating the convergence of high-dimensional process parameter optimization for complex blades. Furthermore, the DecePFL framework is constructed, which achieves personalized federated learning (PFL) through parameter decoupling and performs decentralized federated aggregation, thereby ensuring the privacy protection of industrial data. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conduct experiments on three series of aviation turbine blades (Blade A, Blade B, and Blade C). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves optimization efficiency, reducing optimization iterations from 84 to 27 for Blade A, from 80 to 28 for Blade B, and from 90 to 38 for Blade C.

title: Chat with the manufacturing process: A knowledge-guided cross-modal large language model for machining condition predictive maintenance
abstract: Predictive maintenance for manufacturing processes has become critically urgent to enhance system reliability in modern manufacturing. This paper proposes a cross-modal large language model for conversational diagnosis of machining process, where an interactive decision-making system that integrates multi-source sensor data fusion and knowledge enhancement was constructed. Firstly, the study introduces a knowledge guided graph fusion method to address challenges in information integration. Secondly, a cross-modal image–text generation model is developed to achieve low-parameter alignment between time-series imaging features and language models, enabling the generation of interpretable diagnostic reports. Finally, to tackle knowledge fragmentation issues of general large language models in industrial scenarios, a domain knowledge graph is constructed, covering tool wear mechanisms and the impact of machining parameters. A parameter-efficient fine-tune strategy is employed to inject structured knowledge, mitigating knowledge hallucination issues inherent in general large models. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves an accuracy of 94.2% in tool remaining useful life prediction tasks, representing a 11% improvement over traditional deep learning models, while providing dynamic maintenance recommendations through natural language interaction. This research offers theoretical support for the development of human–machine collaborative machining systems in intelligent manufacturing, advancing online monitoring technologies toward interpretable and interactive paradigms.

title: Deep transfer learning with graph neural networks for the selection of manufacturing processes
abstract: The quality of process planning, linking product design and manufacturing, critically depends on selecting suitable manufacturing processes. In recent years, several deep learning approaches have been proposed for selecting manufacturing processes, frequently relying on synthetically created datasets. While such datasets allow models to capture general manufacturing patterns, they fail to reflect the complexity and variability of industrial 3D CAD models. As a result, the effectiveness of deep learning for predicting manufacturing processes is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality, annotated industrial data. To mitigate the effort for annotation of industrial data, this paper investigates deep transfer learning for the selection of manufacturing processes. Models are first pre-trained on a synthetically designed dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on smaller sets of real industrial data. The findings demonstrate that deep transfer learning enables improved performance in the selection of manufacturing processes.

title: CA-DLM: Causal-aware diffusion language model for interpretable industrial defective image generation
abstract: This research proposes a Causal-Aware Diffusion Language Model (CA-DLM) for interpretable generation of defective images to address the scarcity of defective samples in industrial settings. Firstly, a causal inference mechanism is integrated into DLM to establish a causal mapping among “natural language instructions, model causal variables, and defective image generation”. The counterfactual causal intervention strategy enables interpretable, fine-grained control over defect, texture, and background features during image generation. Secondly, a learnable Structural Causal Model (SCM) is constructed to disentangle semantic features into causal and non-causal variables, effectively separating useful semantic features from confounders during image generation. A causal loss function is also designed to enforce sparsity and acyclicity in the SCM, guiding the model toward a causally consistent structure. Finally, the causal intervention approach is designed to perform do-intervention on SCM to achieve interpretable defective image generation. The do-intervention activates relevant causal variables and suppresses non-causal variables according to the learned SCM, thereby enabling precise control over key defect attributes while preserving the consistency of texture and background. Comparative experiments across three public datasets show that CA-DLM enables interpretable, controllable generation of high-fidelity defective images, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Detection models trained on CA-DLM generated images achieve significant improvements in downstream defect detection tasks, with accuracy exceeding 95%. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing that high-fidelity defective images can be generated using only 30% of causal variables.

title: Integrated dynamic control for production, quality sampling and maintenance in aging manufacturing-remanufacturing facilities
Coordinated optimization of visual inspection and facility layout in PCB manufacturing under bottleneck drift: A DSE-YOLO and EH-SLP-GA framework
Assessment of carrier platform and localization system for autonomous factory inspection
abstract: Autonomous factory inspection increasingly relies on spatially distributed sensing systems to provide consistent and repeatable monitoring in industrial environments. However, inspection outcomes are strongly influenced by the combined effects of carrier platforms, localization accuracy, and sensing characteristics, which are often evaluated in isolation. This paper presents a comparative assessment of carrier platforms and localization systems for autonomous factory inspection, supported by a unified system architecture that integrates heterogeneous carriers, localization methods, multi-modal sensing, and factory layout references. A representative implementation and factory case study evaluate SLAM-based and RTLS-based inspection using mobile and fixed carriers for ambient sensing of noise, illumination, temperature, humidity, and CO₂ concentration. The results show that higher localization accuracy improves the spatial consistency of ambient maps, while different ambient variables exhibit different responses to mobile and static sensing, as sensing behavior varies with carrier mobility and localization uncertainty.

title: Agentic active Asset Administration Shell for circular manufacturing
abstract: The transition to Circular Manufacturing (CM) demands interoperable coordination of heterogeneous Product, Process, and Resource (PPR) data across organizational boundaries and shopfloor systems. Existing semantic technologies for interoperable knowledge representation, such as ontologies and the Asset Administration Shell (AAS), remain passive data carriers decoupled from data integration and operation, while shopfloor orchestration approaches lack grounding in interoperable data standards, leaving a critical gap between structured lifecycle knowledge and closed-loop manufacturing decisions. To resolve this isolation, this paper proposes the Agentic Active AAS (A 4 S), a neural-symbolic architecture that unifies representation, integration, and orchestration within a single framework. A 4 S makes three core contributions. First, A 4 S extends the AAS standard (IEC 63278) from a passive interface to a proactive interoperability layer by leveraging Large Language Models (LLM), which implement the well-known concept of “Active AAS” or “Type3 AAS”. A graph-like recursive encoding of AAS instances is proposed to preserve the strict parent-child topology of AAS shells, submodels, and submodel elements as a symbolic graph traversable by LLM retrieval. Building on this representation, a suite of AAS tools is formalized as the LLM-agent’s bounded action space, enabling the agent to dynamically construct, query, and manipulate AAS instances. Second, A 4 S introduces Agentic Operation Delegation, which abstracts heterogeneous shopfloor operation interfaces into unified AAS operation schemas and mathematically bounds the LLM’s token generation through schema-constrained decoding. Third, building upon the Active AAS layer, an LLM-based Multi-Agent System (LMAS) is developed, in which the Orchestrator Agent and specialized sub-agents interact through the unified AAS substrate. This simultaneously enables automatic creation of Digital Product Passports (DPP) for cross-organizational value chain exchange and intra-enterprise PPR integration for CM operations. The proposed approach is evaluated in a battery remanufacturing scenario with a dynamic system environment. Experimental results show that A 4 S achieves over 95% success rate in complex multi-step shopfloor orchestration tasks, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art LMAS approaches across all model scales. Notably, open-source models (e.g., Qwen3.6–35B) under A 4 S surpass large proprietary models such as GPT-5.2 in orchestration tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed neural-symbolic constraints. For DPP generation, A 4 S-GPT5.2 achieves 90% success rate, where tool execution correctness reaches 100%. These results highlight that A 4 S effectively enables more robust orchestration in the constrained CM environment. The code is released at https://github.com/quickhdsdc/aas-mcp-server.git .

title: Towards data-driven reprocessing: Multisensory process observation and hardness modeling in high-speed directed energy deposition
abstract: The transition towards circular factories requires robust and adaptable manufacturing technologies capable of reprocessing components with highly variable conditions while ensuring consistent quality. High-Speed Directed Energy Deposition with laser beam (HS DED-LB/M) represents a promising approach due to its high productivity, low heat input, and suitability for reprocessing high-value components. However, complex thermo-physical interactions and limited process observability constrain its reliable industrial deployment. In this study, the relationships between process parameters, in-situ multisensory signals, and resulting material properties are systematically investigated for HS DED-LB/M using AISI 4140. A coaxial two color pyrometer is employed to derive temperature-based intermediate feature variables (IFV), which are correlated with hardness. High-speed imaging is used to analyze process dynamics, and Partial Least Squares regression evaluates the predictive capability of process parameters, temperature-based descriptors, and geometry-based descriptors. The results demonstrate high relative densities ( > 99.77%) and small heat-affected zones ( < 40 μ m ), confirming the suitability of HS DED-LB/M for reprocessing. Hardness decreases with increasing laser power, decreasing processing speed, and increasing build height, highlighting the dominant role of global thermal effects. While temperature-based IFV moderately improve hardness prediction, their interpretability is limited by signal superposition effects caused by powder–laser interaction and an oscillating vapor plume. Build height emerges as the most influential descriptor, capturing cumulative thermal effects and significantly improving prediction accuracy. Overall, the results demonstrate that reliable process understanding and prediction in HS DED-LB/M require combining process parameters, in-situ observations, and global thermal history, supporting data-driven, sensor-based approaches for scalable reprocessing in circular factory environments.

title: MARS: Multi-Agent Rescheduling Framework with Large Language Models for Human-Centric Manufacturing
abstract: In manufacturing systems, shop-floor operators frequently adjust algorithmically generated schedules based on their tacit knowledge. However, realizing these modifications through existing interfaces is typically labor-intensive and time-consuming. We identify two fundamental gaps underlying these difficulties: the intent-execution gap and the change-comprehension gap. The intent-execution gap arises from the disparity between high-level user intents expressed in natural language and the sequence of low-level, executable actions required by the existing interfaces. Subsequently, the change-comprehension gap emerges because operators must manually compare the original and modified schedules to recover situational awareness. To address both gaps within a single coherent framework, we propose MARS, a multi-agent rescheduling framework leveraging large language models for human-centric decision support. MARS enables operators to express modification intents directly in natural language, automatically translating them into executable code that updates scheduling parameters or schedules. Designed for computationally constrained manufacturing environments, the framework integrates two agents: a schedule modifier and an explainer. The schedule modifier combines a scheduler re-run classifier and a modification type classifier within a parameter-efficient multi-adapter architecture, and employs a level-wise asymmetric in-context learning (ICL) strategy for the modification code generator. The explainer combines a tree-based causal chain with ICL to describe cascading schedule changes. Experimental results on the unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem demonstrate MARS’s superior ability to accurately execute user requests and generate transparent explanations, alongside robust generalization to larger problems. Ultimately, MARS provides a single natural language interface that effectively supports human decision-making in user-driven rescheduling, bridging both the intent-execution and change-comprehension gaps.

title: A compositional dual-hand action recognition method for LLM-driven assembly assistance
abstract: Effective assistance in manual assembly requires perceiving the operator’s actions in real time and advising the operator flexibly. Traditional action recognition methods classify a video clip into a single holistic label for one action stream, failing to resolve the parallel dual-hand actions or expose the fine-grained semantics for downstream assistance reasoning. Moreover, conventional assistance systems retrieve predefined content keyed to recognized steps and cannot respond to an operator’s situated needs, whereas large language models (LLMs) can respond flexibly but are too slow and hallucination-prone for the real-time, safety-critical path. This paper connects the two through a compositional action representation that expresses each hand’s action as a structured tuple of action verb , manipulated object , target object , and tool . A compositional dual-hand action recognition model, CoDuAR, is proposed to predict the action tuples of both hands in a single forward pass through a shared encoder and hand-specific compositional decoders. On the HA-ViD benchmark, CoDuAR outperforms state-of-the-art recognizers that require a separate model per hand, while using 23% fewer parameters and roughly doubling the dual-hand inference throughput of the strongest parameter-comparable baseline, VideoMAE V2. Built on the compositional representation, a dual-process assistance system, Assembly Copilot, is developed. A deterministic System 1, driven by CoDuAR, maps the predictions to a symbolic task state, tracking the task progression, recommending next tasks, and detecting operational errors in real time, while an LLM-powered agent, System 2, reasons over the symbolic state to answer the operator’s queries and generate post-session performance reviews, gaining flexibility without placing the language model on the latency-critical path. A case study on a gear-plate assembly validates the functionality of the integrated system. The results indicate that the compositional action representation can serve as an effective interface between real-time perception and language-based assembly assistance within the evaluated scenario.

title: Designing multi-view Speed and Separation Monitoring system for multi-robot and multi-human interactions in shared workspace
abstract: Designing multi-view Speed and Separation Monitoring (SSM) systems for multi-robot and multi-human environments remains challenging due to high-dimensional solution space and uncertainties in human behavior. Therefore, this paper presents a novel simulation-driven methodology for multi-view SSM system design that integrates probabilistic modeling of human motion, danger-zone-based safety representation, and voxelized visibility analysis, in multi-robot, multi-human work units. Safety-critical events in the proposed methodology are defined as near-miss human intrusion into dynamically updated robot and end-effector danger zones rather than direct physical contacts. Camera placement optimization is formulated as a joint optimization of positions and orientations to balance coverage, occlusion, and viewpoint diversity. To address the resulting computational complexity, a Parallel Efficient Global Optimization (EGO) approach is adopted to search optimal solution based on computationally expensive digital simulations. The proposed approach is validated in two representative human-robot interaction (HRI) scenarios: a CNC machine tending unit with a single robot and a single human, and palletizing lines with multiple robots and multiple humans. In the CNC machine tending case study, the proposed Parallel EGO method identifies a three-camera layout with no uncovered regions (dark areas) and only 1.25% overall vision occlusions (gray areas). It reduces the number of objective-function evaluations by 74.2% compared with GA and 88.5% compared with NOMAD, while achieving a comparable or lower total loss. In the palletizing case studies, the optimized one-, two-, and three-line layouts requires 3, 6, and 11 cameras, respectively, with dark area percentages of 0%, 0.60%, and 1.43%, and gray area percentages of 6.18%, 14.59%, and 16.36%.

title: Adaptive-fidelity digital twin framework for complex smart manufacturing system
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly adopted in smart manufacturing to enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and decision support. However, deploying high-fidelity digital twins continuously across complex manufacturing systems, characterized by multiple processing stations, heterogeneous machines, and autonomous mobile robots, remains computationally prohibitive. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an Adaptive Fidelity Digital Twin (AFDT) framework that dynamically adjusts simulation fidelity at runtime based on predicted system criticality. The framework integrates three hierarchical fidelity levels: (i) a low-fidelity system-level model for continuous monitoring of aggregate production dynamics, (ii) a medium-fidelity station-level discrete-event model for localized operational diagnosis, and (iii) a high-fidelity machine-level physics-based model for detailed equipment health assessment. An event-triggered fidelity scheduler governs transitions between these levels using manufacturing-relevant indicators such as persistent blockage, starvation, and abnormal resource utilization. The proposed framework is validated through a case study of an automotive parts manufacturing system involving multiple product types and mobile robots. Results demonstrate that the AFDT framework selectively activates high-fidelity models only during disruptive events, achieving substantial reductions in cumulative computational cost compared to static high-fidelity digital twin configurations while preserving diagnostic capability for root-cause analysis. The findings indicate that adaptive fidelity management offers a scalable and computationally efficient approach for operational digital twin deployment in complex manufacturing environments.

title: A pose estimation method for aeroengine blade assembly based on geometric priors and reinforcement learning
abstract: To address the challenges encountered in the automated assembly of aeroengine blades, where non-conformal insertion, irregular boundary features, and insufficient pose alignment accuracy occur between the blade root and disk slot, this paper develops a force-vision-guided robotic assembly platform. Based on the 3D point cloud measured by structured light, a pose estimation method integrating geometric priors (GP) and reinforcement learning (RL) strategies is proposed.
